concepts.title: Public Nutrition and Public Health
concepts.definition: Public health means organised action by society to guard and better the health of whole populations, and public health nutrition applies that group approach to keeping a population well nourished.
concepts.formula: qualitative idea -- population level prevention, not one patient at a time
concepts.key_idea: The mission is two sided: stop undernutrition and overnutrition together and hold the population at optimal status.
concepts.textbook_ref: lehe103.txt, Introduction and What is Public Health Nutrition (approx lines 21-139)
question_patterns: what is public health nutrition
how does public nutrition differ from clinical nutrition and dietetics
why is the word public attached to nutrition and health
what does the double burden of malnutrition mean
define community in the sense used by public health workers
why is public health nutrition called a multidisciplinary field

solution_steps.action: define the population lens
solution_steps.explain: group action targets large numbers, especially vulnerable groups, unlike the single patient focus of clinics

solution_steps.action: state the twin goal: prevent under and overnutrition
solution_steps.explain: India carries both deficits and excess at the same time

worked_examples.q: Organised action by society to guard the health of whole populations is called what health: public or private?

concepts.title: Protein Energy Malnutrition and Growth Failure
concepts.definition: Protein energy malnutrition arises when food energy and protein fall short of needs; it shows up as underweight for age, stunted height for age, or wasted weight for height, with marasmus from energy lack and kwashiorkor from protein lack.
concepts.formula: assessment signs -- weight for age, height for age, weight for height
concepts.key_idea: Children carry the greatest risk, though the elderly and disease patients can also slip into PEM.
question_patterns: explain the terms stunting, wasting and underweight
distinguish between marasmus and kwashiorkor
what is protein energy malnutrition and who faces the greatest risk
how is PEM assessed in a child
which anthropometric signs point to growth retardation in preschoolers

solution_steps.action: define the three growth yardsticks
solution_steps.explain: light for age, short for age, light for height each flag a different failure

solution_steps.action: separate the two severe forms
solution_steps.explain: energy deficit wastes the body; protein deficit swells it with kwashiorkor

worked_examples.q: Which deficiency causes marasmus: energy or protein?

concepts.title: Hidden Hunger: Micronutrient Deficiencies
concepts.definition: Hidden hunger is the quiet shortage of vitamins and minerals -- iron, zinc, vitamin A, C, D, iodine, folic acid and B12 -- that can ride along even when bellies feel full.
concepts.formula: qualitative idea -- enough energy does not guarantee enough micronutrients
concepts.key_idea: An energy and protein poor diet almost always shortchanges minerals and vitamins too.
question_patterns: what is hidden hunger
name the micronutrients of major public health concern in India
why may a diet poor in energy and protein also lack micronutrients
which newly worrying vitamin deficiencies are being watched besides iron and iodine
why are micronutrient gaps called deficiencies of varying severity

solution_steps.action: define the term hidden hunger
solution_steps.explain: the deficit is invisible because calories may be adequate

solution_steps.action: list the watched micronutrients
solution_steps.explain: iron, vitamin A and iodine lead; zinc, B12, folic acid, calcium, D and riboflavin follow

worked_examples.q: The quiet shortage of vitamins and minerals despite full bellies is called what hunger?

concepts.title: Iron Deficiency Anemia
concepts.definition: Iron deficiency anemia is the commonest nutritional disorder worldwide; shortfalls of iron cut hemoglobin output, so oxygen transport suffers and exertion brings breathlessness, fatigue and visible pallor.
concepts.formula: qualitative chain -- low iron to low hemoglobin to poor oxygen carry to fatigue
concepts.key_idea: Women of child bearing age, adolescent girls, pregnant women and school children are the most exposed groups; children also lose attention and memory.
question_patterns: what is iron deficiency anemia and why is it called the most common nutritional disorder
which groups are most vulnerable to IDA
how does a fall in hemoglobin produce breathlessness and fatigue
list the visible signs by which anemia shows itself
how does anemia affect learning in children

solution_steps.action: trace the physiology
solution_steps.explain: reduced hemoglobin manufacture starves muscles and brain of oxygen

solution_steps.action: map the signs: pallor of eyes, tongue, nail beds; lethargy; weak concentration
solution_steps.explain: severity follows the speed of the hemoglobin fall

worked_examples.q: Which is the commonest nutritional disorder worldwide: iron deficiency anemia or scurvy?

concepts.title: Vitamin A Deficiency
concepts.definition: Shortage of vitamin A begins as night blindness and, untreated, ends in total loss of sight; the same deficit lowers immunity and slows growth, and infection in turn drains body stores of the vitamin.
concepts.formula: qualitative cycle -- deficiency to infection to greater losses to deeper deficiency
concepts.key_idea: Vitamin A lack is the leading cause of childhood blindness, and the spiral with infection makes it worse.
concepts.textbook_ref: lehe103.txt, VAD section and vicious cycle figure (approx lines 260-277)
question_patterns: why is vitamin A essential for the body
describe the vicious cycle linking vitamin A deficiency and infection
how does night blindness progress to complete blindness
which deficiency is the most common cause of childhood blindness
name the food sources rich in beta carotene for preventing vitamin A lack

solution_steps.action: list the roles of the vitamin: epithelium, vision, growth, immunity
solution_steps.explain: each role produces its own deficiency sign

solution_steps.action: draw the spiral
solution_steps.explain: deficiency invites infection, infection raises losses, losses deepen the deficiency

worked_examples.q: Vitamin A deficiency begins as which night condition: night blindness or sleepwalking?

concepts.title: Iodine Deficiency Disorders
concepts.definition: Living on iodine poor soil, whole populations can lack the iodine the thyroid needs; the resulting spectrum runs from goitre in adults to cretinism and irreversible mental retardation in children born to deficient mothers.
concepts.formula: qualitative chain -- iodine poor soil to low thyroid hormone to goitre or cretinism
concepts.key_idea: Iodised salt is the classic fortification answer; Himalayan and peninsular belts carry the highest risk.
question_patterns: what are iodine deficiency disorders
why is IDD called an ecological phenomenon
how does iodine lack affect the thyroid gland
distinguish between goitre and cretinism
why is iodine deficiency during pregnancy especially dangerous
name the states where IDD is common in India

solution_steps.action: trace the cause: soil lacking iodine gives iodine lacking crops and diets
solution_steps.explain: the thyroid cannot synthesise enough hormone

solution_steps.action: map the spectrum: enlarged thyroid in adults, cretinism and fetal damage in the next generation
solution_steps.explain: the fetal damage cannot be undone, which is why fortification is universal

worked_examples.q: Iodine shortage in adults shows as which visible swelling: goitre or rash?

concepts.title: Causes of Undernutrition: Three Levels
concepts.definition: Undernutrition is read through three nested layers: immediate causes at the individual (faulty intake and disease), underlying causes at the household (food access, care, water, health services, education), and basic societal causes (resources, political and cultural systems, environment).
concepts.formula: causal ladder -- immediate plus underlying plus basic causes produce malnutrition outcomes
concepts.key_idea: Poverty and poor sanitation sit upstream; no single fix can break the chain alone.
concepts.textbook_ref: lehe103.txt, Fig 3.1 and surrounding text (approx lines 140-217)
question_patterns: explain the three levels of causes behind undernutrition
which immediate causes operate at the level of the individual
name the underlying causes that act at the household level
what basic causes does society contribute to malnutrition
how do poor sanitation and unsafe water feed into lost working days and economic loss

solution_steps.action: order the ladder from individual to society
solution_steps.explain: diet and disease act first, household conditions next, structures last

solution_steps.action: show the interactions
solution_steps.explain: poverty shrinks access to food, toilets and clinics, and the losses circle back as lower earnings

worked_examples.q: Faulty intake and disease are which level causes of undernutrition: immediate or basic?

concepts.title: Food-Based versus Nutrient-Based Strategies
concepts.definition: Food based strategies fight deficiency by putting micronutrient rich foods on the plate through diversification, home gardens, education and fortification, while the nutrient based or medicinal route hands out supplements to at risk groups for a short term.
concepts.formula: strategy choice -- food based is sustainable and safe, supplements are fast but costly
concepts.key_idea: Supplementation cannot cause toxicity through food, works for every household, and is the long term goal; pills reach fewer people and can be overdosed.
question_patterns: compare food based and nutrient based strategies for tackling malnutrition
why are diet based approaches called sustainable
what are the advantages and drawbacks of nutrient supplementation
how does fortification of salt with iodine work as a strategy
what is dietary diversification and why does it need agricultural policy change
which strategy should be the long term goal and why

solution_steps.action: define each strategy family
solution_steps.explain: one changes the plate, the other adds pills and drops

solution_steps.action: weigh them on cost, coverage, sustainability and toxicity
solution_steps.explain: food based win on sustainability and safety; supplements win on speed for targeted groups

worked_examples.q: Putting micronutrient-rich foods on the plate is which strategy: food based or medicinal?

concepts.title: Government Nutrition Programmes
concepts.section: Nutrition programmes operating in our country
concepts.definition: India runs five programme families: ICDS for mother and child care, national deficiency control programmes for vitamin A, anemia and iodine, food supplementation such as the mid day meal, food security through PDS and allied schemes, and employment schemes as social safety nets.
concepts.formula: programme map -- ICDS plus deficiency control plus meal plus food security plus employment
concepts.key_idea: POSHAN Abhiyaan overlays all of these with convergence, targeting stunting, anemia and low birth weight district by district.
concepts.textbook_ref: lehe103.txt, POSHAN Abhiyaan and programme list (approx lines 303-483)
question_patterns: name the five types of nutrition programmes running in India

under which programme is the mid day meal classified

solution_steps.action: classify the programmes into their five families
solution_steps.explain: each family answers a different rung of the causal ladder

solution_steps.action: place POSHAN Abhiyaan as the converging umbrella
solution_steps.explain: it reviews and scales the others district by district

worked_examples.q: Which programme delivers mother and child care through the anganwadi: ICDS or NSS?

concepts.title: Three Levels of Health Care
concepts.definition: India arranges care in a ladder: primary centres as the first contact for families, district hospitals and community centres as the first referral level, and medical colleges and specialised institutes at the top for the hardest cases.
concepts.formula: referral ladder -- primary to secondary to tertiary
concepts.key_idea: Each level handles what the one below cannot; community health centres open the referral chain.
question_patterns: name the three levels at which health care is delivered in India
which institutions form the first level of contact with the health system
what is meant by the first referral level
give examples of tertiary level health institutions
how do community health centres fit into the referral chain

solution_steps.action: define each level and its setting
solution_steps.explain: PHCs, district and community centres, then medical college and specialised hospitals

solution_steps.action: explain the referral flow upward
solution_steps.explain: complexity rises with each step up the ladder

worked_examples.q: Which level of care is the family's first contact: primary or tertiary?

concepts.title: Low Birth Weight Arithmetic
concepts.definition: When a stated fraction of newborns arrive weighing under 2.5 kg, the expected number of low birth weight babies in any birth cohort is that fraction of the total births.
concepts.key_idea: About one Indian infant in five is born under 2.5 kg, a burden that shadows health across the whole life span.
question_patterns: if one fifth of infants are low birth weight, how many such babies are expected among 8000 births in a district
given the low birth weight share and the number of births, calculate the count of babies under 2.5 kg

compute the number of low birth weight infants when the birth cohort and the affected fraction are stated
how many of 350 newborns would be predicted to weigh below 2.5 kg if a fifth are affected

solution_steps.action: apply the low birth weight fraction to the cohort
solution_steps.explain: multiply total births by the affected share

worked_examples.q: Low birth weight is defined below how many kilograms: 2.5 or 5?

concepts.title: POSHAN District Rollout
concepts.definition: POSHAN Abhiyaan phased its district coverage over three years; the combined first two phases come from adding the year one and year two district counts.
concepts.key_idea: Year one took 315 districts and year two another 235, with the remainder following in year three.

solution_steps.action: add the two phase counts
solution_steps.explain: year one plus year two gives the districts already inside the mission after two phases

worked_examples.q: POSHAN Abhiyaan's year one covered how many districts: 315 or 31?

concepts.title: Malnutrition Productivity Loss
concepts.definition: Economists attach a percentage drag to malnutrition: apply the quoted percent to a person's lifetime earnings, or to the nation's GDP, to price the output that poor nutrition destroys.
concepts.key_idea: Losses run past ten percent of individual lifetime earnings and two to three percent of GDP, so fighting malnutrition is an investment.
concepts.textbook_ref: lehe103.txt, costs of malnutrition paragraph (approx lines 66-74)
question_patterns: if productivity losses equal 10 percent of lifetime earnings, how much is lost by a worker earning 400000 rupees over a lifetime

find the rupee value of output lost when the loss rate and the earnings base are given
work out the national cost of malnutrition as a percentage applied to the GDP figure

solution_steps.action: apply the loss rate to the earnings base
solution_steps.explain: multiply the base by the percentage and divide by one hundred

worked_examples.q: Malnutrition losses run past ten percent of individual lifetime what: earnings or height?

concepts.title: Costing a Supplementary Recipe
concepts.section: Practical 1: supplementary foods for nutrition programmes
concepts.definition: A low cost Anganwadi recipe is costed by adding the prices of its ingredients for the full batch and dividing by the number of servings, then checked against the per serving cost limit set by the teacher.
concepts.key_idea: Plans target five servings within Rs 5 a serving, so costing decides which recipe gets cooked.
question_patterns: a supplementary mix uses rice worth Rs 12, dal worth Rs 18 and oil worth Rs 5 for a 5 serving batch; find the cost per serving
calculate the per serving cost of a recipe whose ingredients for the whole batch are priced and the serving count is given
an Anganwadi recipe costs Rs 40 for 5 servings; does each serving stay within the Rs 5 limit
find the serving cost when three ingredient prices are added and divided across the planned servings
work out whether a group's planned recipe respects the teacher's cost cap per serving

solution_steps.action: total the ingredient prices for the batch
solution_steps.explain: every item bought for the recipe enters the batch cost

solution_steps.action: divide by the planned servings
solution_steps.explain: the quotient is the per serving cost to compare with the cap

worked_examples.q: Recipe costing divides the batch price by the number of what: servings or cooks?
